pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src/components/report/useReportScan.ts:421 The report client renders only the server's own error sentence and branches on its closed code (NOT_FOUND), and the GitHub-side network error that used to put the internal GHES host into that sentence is now logged on the server and replaced with a fixed message, so the earlier deviation is fixed.

techniques.evidence: src/components/report/useReportScan.ts:421 The client branches on the closed GitHubError code, and the message it renders now comes from fixed sentences. src/lib/github/source.ts:307-313 now logs the raw fetch error with console.warn and throws "Couldn't reach GitHub. Please try again." instead of interpolating String(e). GraphQL error bodies, which graphql.ts:124-143 copies into messages, are caught and set to null at scan-ingest.ts:157-162, so they never reach the stream.

src/components/report/useReportScan.ts:273 The browser sends only its intent (url, ref, subPath, fresh) to a same-origin route. The GitHub token or installation token is attached on the server, and the body carries no credential.

src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx:259 Read access is decided in app code on the server (canReadOrg), not by store row policies that a browser-held key reaches. This is the technique's 'your code is the only client' exclusion.

src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx:49 Scan rows are read by a server component through @/lib/db. No public role can compose its own query against the table, so this context has no regime-one table shape to judge.
src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/opengraph-image.tsx:34 The share card reads on the server under a resolved readable org. The browser has no grant on a base table, so no aggregate view is needed.
